problem.summary: 如何在没有监督的情况下学习鲁棒的、通用的视觉特征，使其能够跨图像分布和任务工作，无需微调。

motivation.summary: 受自然语言处理中大规模预训练模型成功的启发，计算机视觉领域也需要类似的“基础模型”。现有的文本引导预训练方法（如CLIP）受限于文本描述的丰富性，且需要对齐的文本-图像数据。自监督学习方法有望产生通用特征，但需要在大规模、多样化的数据上训练才能实现。

core_idea.summary: 通过结合和改进现有的自监督学习方法（如iBOT），在精心策划的大规模多样化数据集（LVD-142M）上训练大型Vision Transformer（ViT）模型，并通过知识蒸馏得到一系列更小的模型，从而生成强大的、无需微调的通用视觉特征。

method.summary: 1. 数据构建：构建自动化的数据筛选和再平衡管道，从大量未策划的图像中构建一个多样化、精心策划的142M图像数据集（LVD-142M）。2. 模型训练：基于iBOT等自监督方法，改进训练配方（如超参数、正则化），以稳定和加速大规模训练。训练一个1B参数的ViT-g模型。3. 知识蒸馏：将训练好的ViT-g模型作为教师，通过蒸馏得到一系列更小的模型（如ViT-S/B/L）。

experiments.summary: 在多个视觉任务上评估DINOv2模型，包括图像分类（ImageNet-1k）、语义分割（ADE20K）、深度估计、实例检索、视频动作识别等。与现有的自监督（如DINO, iBOT）和弱监督（如OpenCLIP）模型进行广泛比较。

claims.claim: DINOv2在大多数基准测试中超越了现有的自监督方法，并达到了与弱监督方法相当的性能。
DINOv2生成的特征是通用的，无需微调即可在图像和像素级别的任务上表现良好。
精心策划的大规模多样化数据对于训练强大的自监督视觉特征至关重要。
知识蒸馏是获得高效小模型的有效方法。
DINOv2的训练效率（速度、内存）相比类似方法有显著提升。
DINOv2在地理和标签关联公平性方面表现良好。

limitations.limitation: 论文未明确讨论模型的局限性，但根据内容可推断：1. 训练需要巨大的计算资源（碳排放）。2. 模型性能可能依赖于特定的数据筛选管道。3. 与文本引导模型相比，在某些依赖文本语义的任务上可能仍有差距。

nodes.title: 数据构建管道
nodes.label: 数据准备
nodes.summary: 构建一个自动化的管道，从未策划的图像集合中筛选和再平衡，以创建多样化、精心策划的预训练数据集LVD-142M。
nodes.description: 该管道借鉴了NLP中的数据清洗方法，利用数据相似性而非外部元数据。通过聚类等方法解决概念不平衡问题，避免过拟合到少数主导模式。

nodes.title: 自监督预训练方法
nodes.label: 模型训练
nodes.summary: 基于iBOT等判别式自监督学习方法，进行改进以稳定和加速大规模训练。训练一个1B参数的ViT-g模型。
nodes.description: 改进包括更好的超参数、正则化等。训练过程旨在同时学习图像级和patch级特征。技术贡献主要针对在模型和数据规模扩大时稳定和加速训练。

nodes.title: 知识蒸馏
nodes.label: 模型压缩
nodes.summary: 将训练好的大型ViT-g模型作为冻结的教师模型，通过蒸馏得到一系列更小的模型（如ViT-S/B/L）。
nodes.description: 蒸馏过程中，保留学生模型的EMA作为最终模型，移除掩码和随机深度，并在两个全局裁剪上应用iBOT损失。蒸馏后的模型在所有基准上都优于从头训练的模型。

nodes.title: 损失函数组合
nodes.label: 训练目标
nodes.summary: 结合了iBOT的损失（包括图像级和掩码图像建模损失）以及KoLeo损失，以优化特征学习。
nodes.description: KoLeo损失有助于改善最近邻搜索任务（如检索），而掩码图像建模损失对patch级任务（如分割）至关重要。消融实验证明了这些损失项的重要性。

nodes.title: 模型评估
nodes.label: 评估
nodes.summary: 在广泛的视觉任务上评估DINOv2模型，包括图像分类、语义分割、深度估计、实例检索、视频动作识别等。
nodes.description: 评估使用线性探测（冻结骨干网络）和微调两种方式。与现有的自监督和弱监督基线模型进行比较，以验证特征的通用性和性能。

deltas.before: 使用标准或未精心策划的大规模数据集（如ImageNet-22k）进行训练。
deltas.after: 构建并使用自动化的数据筛选和再平衡管道，创建多样化、精心策划的LVD-142M数据集。
deltas.why_it_matters: 精心策划的多样化数据对于学习通用、鲁棒的视觉特征至关重要，尤其是在模型规模扩大时，其效益更加明显。

deltas.before: 自监督训练在大规模模型和数据上可能不稳定或效率低下。
deltas.after: 改进训练配方（超参数、正则化等），使训练速度提升约2倍，内存需求减少约3倍，从而能够利用更长的训练时间和更大的批量大小。
deltas.why_it_matters: 这些改进使得在更大规模上进行训练成为可能，从而获得性能更好的模型。

deltas.before: 通常从头训练所有模型。
deltas.after: 对于小模型，使用知识蒸馏从大型ViT-g模型中学习，而不是从头训练。
deltas.why_it_matters: 蒸馏得到的小模型在所有基准上都优于从头训练的模型，有时甚至超过蒸馏目标，是一种高效获得高性能小模型的方法。

deltas.before: 损失函数可能侧重于单一目标（如仅图像级对比或仅掩码图像建模）。
deltas.after: 组合使用iBOT损失（图像级和掩码图像建模）与KoLeo损失，以同时优化图像级和patch级特征，并改善特征空间分布。
deltas.why_it_matters: KoLeo损失显著提升了实例检索性能，掩码图像建模损失对密集预测任务（如分割）至关重要，组合损失使特征更通用。

variables.name: L_{iBOT}
variables.description: iBOT损失，包含图像级对比损失和掩码图像建模损失。

variables.name: L_{KoLeo}
variables.description: KoLeo正则化损失，用于改善特征空间分布，促进最近邻搜索。

formulas.intuition: 总损失结合了iBOT的判别性学习目标（学习图像和patch的表示）和KoLeo的正则化目标（使特征在空间中更均匀分布，利于检索）。消融实验表明，KoLeo损失对检索任务提升显著，而iBOT的掩码建模损失对分割等密集任务至关重要。
知识蒸馏过程使用与预训练相同的iBOT损失，但教师模型是冻结的。学生模型学习模仿教师模型的输出。论文提到蒸馏过程移除了掩码和随机深度，并在两个全局裁剪上应用损失。

main_result.description: 在ImageNet-1k上使用线性探测评估冻结特征的Top-1准确率。
main_result.result: DINOv2模型（如ViT-g）显著超越所有自监督基线，并达到或超过最佳弱监督模型（如OpenCLIP）的性能。

main_result.description: 在多个下游任务（分割、深度估计、检索等）上的综合评估。

metadata.title: DINOv2: Learning Robust Visual Features without Supervision
metadata.abstract: The recent breakthroughs in natural language processing for model pretraining on large quantities of data have opened the way for similar foundation models in computer vision. These models could greatly simplify the use of images in any system by producing all-purpose visual features, i.e., features that work across image distributions and tasks without finetuning. This work shows that existing pretraining methods, especially self-supervised methods, can produce such features if trained on enough curated data from diverse sources. We revisit existing approaches and combine different techniques to scale our pretraining in terms of data and model size. Most of the technical contributions aim at accelerating and stabilizing the training at scale. In terms of data, we propose an automatic pipeline to build a dedicated, diverse, and curated image dataset instead of uncurated data, as typically done in the self-supervised literature. In terms of models, we train a ViT model (Dosovitskiy et al., 2020) with 1B parameters and distill it into a series of smaller models that surpass the best available all-purpose features, OpenCLIP (Ilharco et al., 2021) on most of the benchmarks at image and pixel levels.

1 Introduction

Learning task-agnostic pretrained representations have become the standard in Natural Language Process- ing (NLP) (Radford et al., 2019; Raffel et al., 2020; Chowdhery et al., 2022; Hoffmann et al., 2022; Touvron et al., 2023). One can use these features “as they are”, i.e., without fine-tuning, and achieve performances on downstream tasks that are significantly better than those produced by task-specific models (Brown et al.,
2020). This success has been fueled by pretraining on large quantities of raw text using pretext objectives,

such as language modeling (Radford et al., 2017) or word vectors (Devlin et al., 2019), that require no supervision. Following this paradigm shift in NLP, we expect similar “foundation” models to appear in computer vi- sion (Bommasani et al., 2021). These models should generate visual features that work out of the box on any task, both at the image level, e.g., image classification, and pixel level, e.g., segmentation. Most promis- ing efforts towards these foundation models focus on text-guided pretraining, i.e., using a form of textual supervision to guide the training of the features (Joulin et al., 2016; Mahajan et al., 2018; Radford et al., All the authors are affiliated to Meta, except Julien Mairal who is affiliated to Inria. This form of text-guided pretraining limits the information that can be retained about the image since captions only approximate the rich information in images, and complex pixel-level information may not surface with this supervision. Furthermore, these image encoders require aligned text-image corpora and hence, do not offer the flexibility of their text counterparts, that is, to learn from raw data alone. An alternative to text-guided pretraining is self-supervised learning (Caron et al., 2018; Chen et al., 2020; He et al., 2022) where features are learned from images alone. A major difficulty when dealing with images in the wild is to rebalance concepts and avoid overfitting on a
few dominant modes. In this work, a naive clustering approach works reasonably well to resolve this issue.

2 Related Work

Intra-image self-supervised training. A first family of self-supervised methods focuses on pretext tasks built from the image, i.e., extracting a signal from the image to be predicted from the rest of the image. This idea has become prevalent with the work of Doersch et al. (2015), where they train by predicting the context of a given patch. Many other pretext tasks were introduced based on, for example, re-colorizing images (Zhang et al., 2016), predicting transformations (Gidaris et al., 2018), inpainting (Pathak et al., 2016) or patch re-ordering (Noroozi & Favaro, 2016; Misra & Maaten, 2020). Recently, the emergence of patch-based architectures, like ViTs, has led to a revisit of inpainting for pre-training (He et al., 2022; Bao et al., 2021; El-Nouby et al., 2021), potentially in feature space (Assran et al., 2023; Baevski et al., 2022). Of particular interest, He et al. (2022) show that a masked auto-encoder (MAE) learns features that provide substantial improvements when finetu...
Discriminative self-supervised learning. The second line of work, closer to ours, is using discriminative

signals between images or groups of images to learn features. This family of methods has roots in early deep learning work (Hadsell et al., 2006) but became popular with the emergence of instance classification methods (Dosovitskiy et al., 2016; Bojanowski & Joulin, 2017; Wu et al., 2018). 3 Data Processing
We assemble our curated LVD-142M dataset by retrieving, from a large pool of uncurated data, images that

We describe below the main components in our data pipeline including the curated/uncurated data sources, the image deduplication step and the retrieval system. Our pipeline does not require any metadata or text and directly works with images, as shown in Fig. 3. We refer the reader to appendix A for more details on our approach. Data sources. Our selection of curated datasets is detailed in the appendix (Table 15) and contains ImageNet-22k, the train split of ImageNet-1k, Google Landmarks and several fine-grained datasets. For the 4

This results in 1.2B unique images. Deduplication. We apply the copy detection pipeline of Pizzi et al. (2022) to the uncurated data and remove near-duplicate images. This reduces redundancy and increases diversity among images. We also remove near-duplicates of images contained in the test or validation set of any benchmark used in this work. 5 Efficient implementation
We consider several improvements to train models at a larger scale. We train models on A100 GPUs using

PyTorch 2.0. The code and pretrained models are made available under Apache 2.0 license1. The details of our models are in the appendix, Table 17. With the same hardware, compared to the iBOT implementation, the DINOv2 code runs around2×faster using only1/3 of the memory. Fast and memory-efficient attention.We implemented our own version of FlashAttention (Dao et al., 2022) to improve memory usage and speed on the self-attention layers. Our version is on par with or better than the original on all cases considered, while covering more use-cases and hardware. Due to the GPU hardware specifics, the efficiency is best when the embedding dimension per head is a multiple of 64, and the matrix operations are even better when the full embedding dimension is a multiple of 256. As a consequence, our ViT-g architecture slightly differs from the architecture proposed by Zhai et al.
(2022) in order to maximize compute efficiency, and we use an embedding dimension of 1536 with 24 heads
(64 dim/head), rather than 1408 with 16 heads (88 dim/head). Our experiments did not show significant differences in final accuracy, and our ViT-g backbone counts 1.1B parameters.
Sequence packing. The DINO algorithm requires forwarding both large crops (at resolution 224) and

small crops (resolution 98). When split into patches, these two groups are represented by token sequences of different lengths and cannot be forwarded together. In order to accelerate training, we use a trick called "sequence packing," which originates from NLP (Krell et al., 2022). This way, the forward is strictly equivalent to forwarding each sequence separately. This trick gives us significant compute efficiency gains compared to using separate forward and backward passes, as in prior implementations. 9 Estimating the Environmental Impact of Training our Models
Training foundation models consumes a significant amount of energy, resulting in carbon dioxide emissions.
Patterson et al. (2021) propose a methodology to report an estimation of the carbon emitted during the

training of a model based on the specifics of the data center and its power grid. This computation informs the design of the data center used for the training of models and the choice of location for data centers.
This methodology requires to know the specifics of the data center used for training, which can be complex
when multiple data centers are involved over time. Additionally, these specifics are most often not in the
control of the AI practitioner, and hence, this methodology is less helpful when practioners make technical
decisions about future trainings. Instead, in this section, we follow an alternative that reports the potential
carbon emission of retraining a similar model in an average data center located in the US. This methodology

was used in previous work in natural language processing (Strubell et al., 2019; Touvron et al., 2023) to establish an apple-to-apple comparison between pretraining schemes. More precisely, we fix the value of all exogenous variables, i.e., the Power Usage Effectiveness (PUE) and carbon intensity factor of a power grid to the same values as in Touvron et al. (2023), that is, a PUE of 1.1 and the carbon intensity factor to the US average of 0.385 kg CO2eq/KWh. We use the same formula as in Patterson et al. (2021) to estimate the potential energy consumption and the carbon emission. For the power consumption of an A100-80GB, we take the thermal design power for NVLink systems, which is 400W. 10 Future work and Discussion
In this work, we present DINOv2, a new series of image encoders pretrained on large curated data with no

supervision. This is the first SSL work on image data that leads to visual features that close the performance gap with (weakly) supervised alternatives across a wide range of benchmarks and without the need for finetuning. We can attribute the strong performance of the DINOv2 family of models to several factors:
i) an improved training recipe with better hyperparameters and regularization (Table 1),ii) a larger model
scale with improved results regardless of the data used for training (Fig. 4),iii) a larger dataset (Fig. 4)

and iv) the distillation process that makes smaller models benefit from the performance of the strongest ViT-g model (Fig. 5). A few properties emerge from these models, such as an understanding of object parts and scene geometry regardless of the image domains. We expect that more of these properties will emerge
at larger scales of models and data, akin to instruction emergence in large language models, and plan to

continue scaling along these axes. This paper also demonstrates that these visual features are compatible with classifiers as simple as linear layers - meaning the underlying information isreadily available. In future work, we plan to leverage this ability to train a a language-enabled AI system that can process visual features as if they were word tokens, and extract the required information to ground the system. sample-based, applies to datasets larger than 1M images and consists in collecting a fixed numberk of nearest
images for each sample image of the dataset to retrieve, effectively trying to multiply byk the size of the
dataset. We usek = 4 for Google Landmarks v2 and ImageNet-22k but a largerk = 32 to make this specific

retrieval a core part of our LVD-142M dataset. For smaller datasets, the second approach, cluster-based, consists in first clustering our uncurated data source into100,000 separate clusters thanks to a distributed k-means implementation. Each cluster should capture different types of image concept and contents. We then pick 10,000 images from each cluster associated with more than3 images of the retrieved dataset. As
this can result in a very large number of retrieved images for some dataset, we restrict such retrievals to a
maximum of 1M images to maintain the balance between the different datasets within LVD-142M.
